test: B3a: HU-frontier factorization vs monolithic 3-way CFR on a reduced game that fits in memory

reduced_game.chance: uniform over the listed cards (1/3 each); combos colliding with a dealt card lose their mass (identical definition in A and B)
reduced_game.menu: M2 (50% bet, raise all-in, 1 raise/street, 0.85 threshold, no donk)
reduced_game.card_removal: exact between all three hands (folded players keep blocking)

A_monolithic: t2_3way solve, all nodes updated every iteration, DCFR(1.5,0,2), alternating over the 3 players, 400 iterations, evaluation every 50

B_factorized.frontier: the 2-active subtree below a fold at a 3-active node
per_trunk_iteration: arriving reaches of ALL frontiers from that snapshot
solve each frontier HU subgame 100 DCFR iterations (exact game: the folded player blocks)
update the trunk (all 3 players, alternating) with frontier values from the frontier average strategies
B_factorized.no_sequential_updates: no frontier is solved after the trunk has changed within a trunk iteration

pass_criteria_fixed_before_running.conservation: |sum of range values - pot| <= 1e-6 in A and B
pass_criteria_fixed_before_running.class_values: mean over classes |A - B| <= 0.05 bb per player
pass_criteria_fixed_before_running.action_frequency: aggregate frequencies at the first decision of each player on the check line and after a flop bet: |A - B| <= 0.05
pass_criteria_fixed_before_running.convergence: per-player BR gain decreasing in both A and B over the checkpoints (same direction)
pass_criteria_fixed_before_running.rerun: A and B re-run for 50 iterations twice: identical results (deterministic; no sampling in either)

measurements: fast O(52N)-type 3-player evaluator: per-call time vs the O(N^2) one, max relative difference vs brute force
per-iteration time A and B, split trunk vs HU re-solve
extrapolation to the full node 46 game (memory and 100-iteration time) from measured per-call costs and B1 counts
if_fail: no node 46 B3 solve; the failing component is isolated first
